# pangolin_role (Resource)

Manages a Pangolin role. Roles carry both standard RBAC fields (`name`, `description`) and the SSH bastion configuration: whether members of this role may open SSH sessions through Pangolin, how sudo is gated, which Unix groups to grant on the target host, and whether to auto-create a home directory.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pangolin_role" "developers" {
  name        = "developers"
  description = "Access for the development team"

  # SSH bastion: allow members to open SSH sessions through Pangolin,
  # with command-restricted sudo and explicit Unix groups on the target host.
  allow_ssh           = true
  ssh_create_home_dir = true
  ssh_sudo_mode       = "commands"
  ssh_sudo_commands = [
    "/usr/bin/systemctl restart nginx",
    "/usr/bin/journalctl",
  ]
  ssh_unix_groups = ["docker", "kvm"]

  # Require admin approval each time a new device tries to use this role.
  require_device_approval = true

  # On destroy, move the members to the auditors role rather than to the
  # first non-admin role by name. Never an admin role.
  replacement_role_id = pangolin_role.auditors.id
}

# Tighter role: no SSH at all, view-only.
resource "pangolin_role" "auditors" {
  name        = "auditors"
  description = "Read-only access for compliance audits"
  allow_ssh   = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the role.

### Optional

- `allow_ssh` (Boolean) Whether members of this role may open SSH sessions through the Pangolin bastion.
- `description` (String) The description of the role.
- `replacement_role_id` (Number) ID of the role that receives the members of this role when it is deleted. It must be another non-admin role of the organization, or the destroy fails without deleting anything. Unset: the first non-admin role by name. Only used on destroy: changing it leaves the role unchanged on the server. When it references another `pangolin_role` (`pangolin_role.other.id`), Terraform destroys this role first, so the replacement still exists.
- `require_device_approval` (Boolean) Require an administrator to approve each new device before its user can use this role. Enterprise: a server without a license ignores it, and the apply fails with an inconsistent result.
- `ssh_create_home_dir` (Boolean) Whether to create the user's home directory on the host when they first log in. Enterprise: a server without a license ignores it, and the apply fails with an inconsistent result.
- `ssh_sudo_commands` (List of String) List of sudo command patterns allowed when `ssh_sudo_mode = "commands"`. Ignored otherwise. Enterprise: a server without a license ignores it, and the apply fails with an inconsistent result.
- `ssh_sudo_mode` (String) How sudo is gated for SSH sessions opened by members of this role. `none` disables sudo, `full` allows any command, `commands` allows only `ssh_sudo_commands`. Enterprise: a server without a license ignores it, and the apply fails with an inconsistent result.
- `ssh_unix_groups` (List of String) Unix groups added to the user account on the host when they log in via SSH. Enterprise: a server without a license ignores it, and the apply fails with an inconsistent result.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The numeric ID of the role.
- `is_admin` (Boolean) Whether this is the built-in admin role of the organization. Admin roles cannot be deleted.
- `org_name` (String) Display name of the organization the role belongs to.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Roles import by numeric ID. Look it up via the pangolin_roles
# data source.
terraform import pangolin_role.example <role_id>
```
